releases.body:
# v0.49.23

This patch makes sure Magic Context's background runs on Oh My Pi can only use the tools they are given.

## Upgrading

- Restart Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- On Oh My Pi, Magic Context's background runs (the summarizer, the dreamer and their helpers) are meant to run with no tools, or with a short read-only list. Oh My Pi applied that restriction to its built-in tools only, so tools from extensions you have installed were still offered to those runs and could be called. Each background run now gets exactly its own tool list, and starts no run at all if the restriction can't be applied. Your extensions still load, so provider and sign-in extensions keep working. Pi was not affected.

# v0.49.22

This patch keeps Oh My Pi summarizer and dreamer runs working when the conversation they read mentions a file or a URL with `@`.

## Upgrading

- Restart Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- Oh My Pi summarizer and dreamer runs no longer fail or attach files when the transcript they read contains `@` mentions such as `@skill://name` or a file path. Mentions stay literal text, and memories they write keep a plain `@` (#779, thanks @Qiiks).

# v0.49.21

This patch makes Pi and Oh My Pi sessions more reliable and releases idle local embedding memory. It also adds optional hosted search reranking and improves documentation-maintenance fallbacks.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode, Pi, or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## New

- Optionally configure hosted `ctx_search` reranking with a user-level [`rerank` block](https://github.com/cortexkit/magic-context/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md); local reranking remains the default (#765, thanks @XWIlluDelu).

## Fixed

- Oh My Pi sessions continue after tag-prefix cleanup, including saved history and forks (#766, thanks @sisttri and @Qiiks).
- Local embedding processes stop after ten idle minutes and restart on demand. OpenCode 2 releases embeddings when their last context closes (#767, thanks @LouisLau-art).
- Documentation maintenance tries the configured fallback model for invalid proposal JSON and recognizes formatted empty proposals as no changes (#768, thanks @breakbeatkid).
- Older Pi and Oh My Pi sessions no longer refuse turns after their first local tag update (#769, thanks @sisttri).
- Pi and Oh My Pi limit database lock waits to the remaining turn budget instead of leaving turns stuck (#770, thanks @andrewsoonqn).
- `map-memories` no longer promises a fallback attempt when the remaining budget cannot allow it (#771, thanks @breakbeatkid).
- Pi sessions no longer refuse turns immediately after another session's slow tag loading fails.
- OpenCode 2 message search keeps up with long sessions, catches up on previously missed messages, and reflects reverted history (#772, thanks @null-axiom).
- Oh My Pi no longer refuses turns after switching models when an earlier reply was interrupted during thinking (#686, thanks @Qiiks for the report and @Zireael for the test case).
- Replies containing only a copied tag no longer send an empty part that strict OpenAI-compatible providers reject, and affected sessions recover automatically (#775, thanks @yongwun).
- Updated Zod to 4.6.7 to address a memory-exhaustion vulnerability in collection validation.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.18
releases.body:
## Dashboard 0.20.18

Reads Broca logs that use three new log features:

- `provider-declarations/v1`: a run's plan manifest records the result formats and `late_results` capability its tool providers declare.
- `provider-held/v1`: held tool-call records and a `tool_held` pause reason.
- `plan-reference-slots/v1`: a run's plan manifest records the reference slots its tools declare.

The dashboard doesn't use these fields. Without this release, it stops reading a Broca log at the first record that requires one of them, and the steps after that point don't show.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.17
releases.body:
## Fixes

- The Broca runs view reads runs from Broca releases that record when each message was written (`message-times/v1`). Before this release, the dashboard stopped reading a run's log at the first such record.
